issues.failure_explanation: By definition, h^{eps,eta}_{0,x}(s) controls increments only through (|w|∨eta)^{gamma_eps}, not |w|^{gamma_eps}. In the proof of (holder-space-gamma), the bound uses |w|^{gamma_eps} and then reduces it to |w|^beta s^{-beta/alpha}. For |w|<eta this step is unjustified: an extra term eta^{gamma_eps} s^{-gamma_eps/alpha} h(s), with no |w|^beta smoothing factor, appears in Delta_3 and Delta_4 and is not estimated.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Carry the (|w|∨eta)^{gamma_eps} factor through the argument. The extra eta-terms are integrated against |nabla^2 p| or |nabla p| on t-s ≥ (|y-y'|∨eta)^alpha. They yield at most (|y-y'|∨eta)^{gamma_eps} times a small power of t multiplying sup h, so the circular argument still closes for small T.
issues.overall_effect: The circular estimate giving uniform-in-eta boundedness of h^{eps,eta}, and hence (holder-space-gamma), is incomplete as written. Theorem thm-main (Delta_6) and the proof of (holder-time-gamma) both use this estimate.
issues.title: Viscosity parameter eta dropped when invoking the circular quantity h^{eps,eta} in the spatial Hölder proof
issues.why_classification: The repair is local bookkeeping within the existing argument. The extra terms carry a small factor, so the method, exponent and conclusion are unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: The statement allows t'-t up to t. In that case the H_32 interval [(2t-t')/2, t-(t'-t)] and the H_33 interval [t-(t'-t), t] both extend down to s near 0. There the comparison bar p(s,y-x) ≲ bar p(t,y-x) fails. The z-independent term bar p(s,y-x)s^{-beta/alpha} then gives a non-integrable singularity near y=x, of order s^{-(d+beta)/alpha}.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the computation to t'-t ≤ t/2, so that all intervals stay in s ≥ t/4. For t/2 < t'-t ≤ t, conclude directly from the Aronson bound (ineq-density-diff), since ((t'-t)/t)^{gamma/alpha} ≳ 1 and bar p(t) ≍ bar p(t') there.
issues.overall_effect: (holder-time-gamma) is not proved as written in the regime t/2 < t'-t ≤ t. Theorem thm-main uses it for Delta_2.
issues.title: Time-Hölder proof compares bar p(s,·) with bar p(t,·) on intervals reaching s≈0
issues.why_classification: A short case split using already available bounds preserves the full statement.

issues.failure_explanation: Since gamma/alpha + 1/alpha = (alpha+beta)/alpha > 1, the integral ∫_h^t s^{-gamma/alpha}(t-s)^{-1/alpha} ds is of order t^{1-(gamma+1)/alpha} = t^{-beta/alpha}. This blows up as t→0, so the claimed bound uniform in t is false.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace (maj-D2-mainthm) by |Delta_2| ≲ t^{-beta/alpha} h^{gamma/alpha} bar p_alpha(t,y-x), which is absorbed into the theorem's prefactor.
issues.overall_effect: The intermediate estimate (maj-D2-mainthm) is wrong as stated. The final bound (BD_THM) already contains the factor (1+t^{-beta/alpha}), so it is unaffected once the correction is made.
issues.title: Delta_2 bound omits the singular factor t^{-beta/alpha}
issues.why_classification: This is a one-line correction with no loss: the theorem's rate and prefactor are unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: In the scheme term, the gradient is evaluated at X^h_s, not at X^h_{tau_s}. Conditioning gives the kernel nabla p(t-tau_s, y-z-b(r,z)(s-tau_s)), whose z-integral does not vanish because the shift depends on z. The cancellation via (USEFUL_FOR_DELTA_6) is therefore applied to the wrong kernel. Without cancellation one only gets order h^{(alpha-1)/alpha}, which is worse than h^{gamma/alpha}.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the correct conditional kernel nabla p(t-tau_s, y-z-b(r,z)(s-tau_s)) and insert the same pivot as for Delta_43, freezing the drift at b(r,y). The pivot term is bounded by (s-tau_s)(t-tau_s)^{(beta-2)/alpha} times bar p and is integrable over the last steps, giving at least h^{gamma/alpha}.
issues.overall_effect: The estimate (maj-D6-mainthm) for the last time steps is not established as written, so the h^{gamma/alpha} rate of thm-main is unsupported on [tau_t^h-h, t].
issues.title: Delta_62 represented with X^h_s replaced by X^h_{tau_s}, making the cancellation invalid as written
issues.why_classification: The fix repeats an argument already in the paper (the Delta_43 pivot) and preserves the stated rate and prefactor.
